summary: McDowell County, WV tower run by the state Division of Forestry; on the telephone by 1926, a 1939 watchman search, listed as gone. No source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association; no source we read describes what remains at the site

events.note: Connected by telephone to the Northfork central office of the Bluefield Telephone Company (Charleston Gazette item, reprinted on Forest Lookouts)
Search for a fire tower watchman missing 36 hours during a new outbreak of forest fires (Steubenville Herald Star item, reprinted on Forest Lookouts)
Registered January 26, 2017 as US 1677, WV 68; nominated by Brian M. Powell

evidence.supports: administered by the West Virginia Division of Forestry
Forest Fire Lookout Association county list marks the tower as gone
evidence.quote: Shawnee Mountain 37.40354 -81.43515 Tower Gone FFLOS US 1677, WV 68

evidence.supports: Charleston Gazette attribution for the 1926 item
tower connected by telephone to the Northfork central office, Bluefield Telephone Company
evidence.quote: The Shawnee Mountain tower in McDowell County is connected with the Northfork central office of the Bluefield Telephone Company.

evidence.supports: November 1939 search for a fire tower watchman missing 36 hours during a new outbreak of forest fires
evidence.quote: November 13, 1939: State Forester Dan Griffin reported today a widespread search in progress for a fire tower watchman missing 36 hours during a new outbreak of forest fires.

evidence.supports: watchman William Thompson could not be reached at his station atop the mountain
evidence.quote: All efforts to reach William Thompson at his station atop Shawnee mountain in McDowell county have failed, Griffin said.

evidence.supports: state police aid enlisted; no search of the area is described
evidence.quote: The official said the aid of the state police has been enlisted.

evidence.supports: Steubenville Herald Star attribution for the 1939 item

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The register and the FFLA county list agree the tower is gone, but no source gives a build date, design, height, or what remains. The 1939 watchman search has no outcome in our sources. Access is not stated. Search hits for 1930s CCC towers at Shawnee National Forest (IL) and Shawnee State Forest (OH) are different places and were not used. A Division of Forestry or McDowell County history check would help.
